design: Binary-monotone acceptance fixed across five search variants. Each cohort has 100 saved validation queries and budgets 5, 10, 20. Shared saliency initializations, 12 additions, 3 removals, 8 steps, single exchanges, original-graph evaluation. Including initialization, each report contains 1800 rows.
interpretation: Small and mixed grouping gains do not establish a consistent independent spectral advantage. Diffusion union and structural union have identical binary outcomes on both cohorts; random union beats diffusion union on two Cora conditions and loses on one PubMed condition. Acceptance-policy improvements must not be attributed to coarsening. This is not an impossibility result or a significance test.
limitations: Previously inspected validation cohorts, not fresh held-out evidence; no test-set tuning.
One grouping seed and one checkpoint per dataset in this study.
Query-budget conditions are dependent, not independent experimental replicates.
Equal per-step proposal caps do not imply equal realized work or equal runtime.
Search-only timings exclude offline grouping, initialization and final evaluation; shared GPU execution is not a controlled end-to-end speed benchmark.
Binary ties do not imply identical supports or continuous confidence metrics.

checks: accepted-step objective gain and binary non-regression

decision: Keep results, including neutral and negative outcomes, in JSON. Do not promote grouping or overwrite historical LaTeX measurements. Further method selection requires validation evidence and controlled cost comparisons; final empirical manuscript updates require a frozen protocol.
